purpose: Give every household necessity and place foundation a clean structural home — housing, health, food, energy, education, mobility, care, aging, disability, and core infrastructure — so Stage 1 skeleton coverage advances without opening research campaigns.

master_architecture_fragment.title: Household & Place Engine
master_architecture_fragment.one_sentence: Constitutional Capitalism treats the household as the unit of prosperity and place as the physical system that makes work, care, learning, health, food, energy, and mobility possible — so ownership, funding, and infrastructure rules must raise household capability without inventing a theoretical society detached from Arkansas today.

flow.label: Land, housing, water, digital, mobility, and energy set where households can live and produce (LOCK-03, LOCK-07)
Food, healthcare, and energy access determine whether wages convert into real security
Education, childcare/family infrastructure, aging, and disability access convert inheritance into capability across the life course (HYP-133)
Household outcomes join Money & Ownership: credit, ownership ladders, and public-income engines fund place without taxing ordinary homes into insecurity (Pass 1)
Delivery agencies, procurement, and transition sequencing live on Pass 3–4 — this spine defines what must be delivered

structural_areas.problem: Housing cost, land speculation, zoning barriers, and insecure tenure dominate household budgets; property-tax dependence ties local finance to a contested base.
structural_areas.objective: Make secure, affordable housing and productive land access normal while preventing speculative capture of community-created land rents.
structural_areas.mechanism: Ownership pathways (including CLT / limited-equity where fit); anti-speculation and vacant-land tools; supply-expanding zoning that preserves community character; property-tax replacement path via Community Prosperity Ledger; working-farm stewardship rewards.
structural_areas.ownership_funding: Households and community vehicles own shelter assets; public/community claim on unearned land-value gains; mortgage/credit from LOCK-02; millage replacement from LOCK-01/06 later.
structural_areas.household_effect: Lower shelter burden, secure tenure, pathway to equity without speculative displacement.

unresolved_deferred.item: Arkansas constitutional constraints on land-value capture

structural_areas.arkansas_baseline_flag: Property / local finance layers already partially bound elsewhere; full millage replacement design stays Pass 3 (LOCK-06) — do not reopen here.

structural_areas.problem: The system finances billable illness transactions more reliably than permanent rural capacity; households face access gaps, medical debt risk, and workforce shortages.
structural_areas.objective: Finance durable health capacity so households can work, learn, and age without medical insecurity destroying surplus.
structural_areas.mechanism: Capacity-first rural health architecture; essential-systems rules for insurance/markets; prevention and primary care as household infrastructure; join to aging and disability accessibility.
structural_areas.ownership_funding: Mix of public capacity investment, community facilities, and market providers under anti-extraction rules (LOCK-05); GR Medicaid/DHS patterns visible in State Baseline — analysis deferred.
structural_areas.household_effect: Access, lower catastrophic risk, more usable time and earnings.

structural_areas.arkansas_baseline_flag: FY2026 DHS ~$1.86B GR allocation is a major touchpoint — flag for Stage 2/3 capability questions; no line-item pass here.

structural_areas.problem: Households face food insecurity while agricultural value often leaves the state before households and communities capture processing surplus.
structural_areas.objective: Secure household nutrition and keep more food-system surplus inside Arkansas communities.
structural_areas.mechanism: Community food security framework; family-farm prosperity; local ownership / hub pathways (HYP-131 food-hub stage closed at first-pass maturity — COUNTABLE $0).
structural_areas.ownership_funding: Local/community ownership of processing and distribution where viable; public share only after free-cash gates; farms as productive household/community assets.
structural_areas.household_effect: Reliable food access; potential local employment and ownership stakes.

unresolved_deferred.item: Facility utilization / operating-statement validation
County-level food-access series completion

structural_areas.arkansas_baseline_flag: Agriculture and DHS nutrition-adjacent spending are baseline-relevant; do not reopen food-hub deep bind.

structural_areas.problem: Households and communities depend on energy systems that can export surplus, impose volatile bills, and leave rural reliability gaps.
structural_areas.objective: Reliable, affordable energy access with ownership and pricing rules that retain productive surplus locally where public assets enable it.
structural_areas.mechanism: Energy sovereignty framework; resource stewardship joins; public participation / cooperative and municipal pathways where markets fail; resilience under shock tests later.
structural_areas.ownership_funding: Mix of utility ownership forms; public claim on rents from public-enabled surplus; Use/Depletion engines (LOCK-01) priced later — not counted now.
structural_areas.household_effect: Bill stability, reliability, reduced energy poverty.

unresolved_deferred.item: County cooperative vs IOU ownership map
Rate-design incidence on low-income households

structural_areas.arkansas_baseline_flag: Utility regulation and capital outlays touch GR/special revenues — normalize later from baseline corpus.

structural_areas.problem: Education is treated as a consumption cost rather than conversion of Arkansas inheritance into greater human capability across generations.
structural_areas.objective: Every generation leaves Arkansas's stock of capability and prosperity larger than it found it — through bona fide residency and public investment (HYP-133), not citizenship rhetoric.
structural_areas.mechanism: Human-capital / education prosperity architecture; intergenerational capital layer; Resident Investment Rate design (legal tests later); Demand Map remains first empirical pass.
structural_areas.ownership_funding: Public educational assets as intergenerational capital; nonresident premiums reflect access value; public IP claim ∝ public contribution (joins Pass 1).
structural_areas.household_effect: Capability, mobility with loyalty pathways, lower credential debt traps for residents.

Three separate legal tests (residency/premium/IP)

structural_areas.arkansas_baseline_flag: FY2026 Education Freedom Accounts $187.5M and ~$777.5M institutions of higher education GR are major patterns — Stage 2/3 capability questions; no EFA policy war inside Pass 2.

structural_areas.problem: Without reliable mobility, households cannot reach work, care, school, or clinics — especially in rural Arkansas.
structural_areas.objective: Guarantee mobility floors that make household participation real across geography.
structural_areas.mechanism: Integrated mobility stack inside LOCK-07: roads, transit, rural mobility options; joins housing location and aging/disability access.
structural_areas.ownership_funding: Public infrastructure ownership with pricing/use rules; capital from state/federal/local mixes; Use engines later — not counted now.
structural_areas.household_effect: Access to jobs and services; lower time poverty.

Transit funding post-property-tax path

structural_areas.arkansas_baseline_flag: Highway/transport appropriations live across GR and dedicated streams — corpus normalize later.

structural_areas.problem: Childcare scarcity and cost block labor participation, firm formation, and early capability formation; family is treated as private residual rather than prosperity infrastructure.
structural_areas.objective: Make family formation and stable caregiving compatible with work, ownership ladders, and community rootedness.
structural_areas.mechanism: Family framework + assistance architecture as household infrastructure; childcare as workforce and human-capital prerequisite; joins HYP-133 early years.
structural_areas.ownership_funding: Public/community capacity mixed with private providers; anti-extraction in care markets; funding joins LOCK-01 engines and LOCK-04 labor — design-level only.
structural_areas.household_effect: Time, earnings, and child capability rise together.

structural_areas.arkansas_baseline_flag: DHS children/family and early-childhood lines are baseline touchpoints — flag only.

structural_areas.problem: Aging often forces asset exhaustion, institutionalization default, and caregiver collapse — destroying household and community surplus.
structural_areas.objective: Prosperous aging: security, participation, and care without impoverishment.
structural_areas.mechanism: Prosperous aging framework; home/community care preference; accessibility joins disability and housing; workforce for care economy.
structural_areas.ownership_funding: Public long-term supports + family/community care capacity; facility ownership rules against extractive chains (LOCK-05).
structural_areas.household_effect: Dignity, retained assets, reduced catastrophic care shocks.

structural_areas.arkansas_baseline_flag: DHS aging/adult behavioral health and related GR lines — Stage 2 capability pull.

structural_areas.problem: Disability and accessibility gaps exclude households from work, education, housing, and civic life — converting treatable barriers into permanent disadvantage.
structural_areas.objective: Equal standing in participation: physical, digital, and service accessibility as default system design.
structural_areas.mechanism: Equal-standing doctrine applied to place systems; accessibility requirements across housing, mobility, digital, education, and care; assistance without dependency traps.
structural_areas.ownership_funding: Public duty to accessible infrastructure; private providers under equal-access rules; funding via general capacity budgets — not a new extractive fee on disabled households.

structural_areas.arkansas_baseline_flag: DDS and related DHS lines are baseline-relevant; no deep bind in Pass 2.

structural_areas.problem: Water, watershed, broadband, and core physical systems determine whether places can host households and enterprise — or become extractive private bottlenecks.
structural_areas.objective: Reliable water stewardship and digital/physical access as shared productive capacity with clear public claim where public assets enable private surplus.
structural_areas.mechanism: LOCK-07 stack: watershed/water rights stewardship; broadband/public-option digital layers where markets fail; cybersecurity baselines for public systems; joins energy and food logistics.
structural_areas.ownership_funding: Public/community ownership of essential access layers where monopoly risk is high; pricing prevents private rents on necessity.
structural_areas.household_effect: Participation in work/school/care; resilience under shock.

os_crosscut_pass_result.ownership: Homes, land, care facilities, food/energy assets, and infrastructure access rights are explicit household/community ownership questions
os_crosscut_pass_result.capital_formation: Education, health capacity, infrastructure, and farm/energy assets are how current surplus becomes future household capability
os_crosscut_pass_result.market_design: Care, food, energy, and housing markets need anti-extraction rules or they destroy household surplus
os_crosscut_pass_result.household_economics: This spine is the household-economics core — income means little if shelter, care, food, energy, and mobility consume it
os_crosscut_pass_result.power: Whoever controls housing, care chains, utilities, and digital access can reconcentrate political power — joins Pass 3
